title: Calling
content:
# Calling

Turn on WhatsApp Business Calling for a connected number, forward calls to a phone, SIP endpoint or AI voice agent, and place outbound calls with the customer's permission.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

By the end of this page, customers can call your WhatsApp number from inside the chat, and the call rings wherever you chose. You can also place calls to customers who allowed it.

## Where calls go

Zernio bridges each call to a `forwardTo` destination:

- a phone number (`tel:`)
- a SIP endpoint such as a Vapi, Retell or ElevenLabs agent (`sip:`)
- a WebSocket media server of your own (`wss:`)

Calling runs on `/v1/phone-numbers/{id}/whatsapp/calling`. The `/v1/whatsapp/phone-numbers/{id}/calling` paths are deprecated aliases.

## What it costs

Both directions meter the carrier connection per minute, plus $0.004/minute when recording is on.

Meta charges its own per-minute rate on outbound calls only, billed directly to your WABA, and nothing on inbound ([WhatsApp rates](/pricing/whatsapp)).

`GET /v1/whatsapp/calls/estimate` with `accountId`, `to` and `minutes` returns the outbound legs before you dial.

## Before you start

You need a connected WhatsApp account with usage-based billing active.

<Callout type="warn">
Meta blocks business-initiated calls on numbers registered in the US, Canada, Egypt, Vietnam and Nigeria; inbound calls to those numbers still work.
</Callout>

Elsewhere, `POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/whatsapp/calling` returns `422` in two cases:

- The team is not on usage-based billing.
- The number's messaging limit is below Meta's ~2,000-daily-recipient threshold.

A new number starts at `TIER_250`. Send messages from it until Meta raises the limit, then enable calling.

## Step 1: Read the calling config

Call `GET /v1/whatsapp/calling` with `accountId`. The response carries `phoneNumberDocId`, the `{id}` every other calling call takes, plus the current destination and recording flag.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();
const accountId = '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d';

const { data: config } = await zernio.whatsappcalling.getWhatsAppCallingConfig({
  query: { accountId }
});

const phoneNumberId = config.phoneNumberDocId;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()
account_id = "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d"

config = client.whatsapp_calling.get_whats_app_calling_config(account_id=account_id)

phone_number_id = config["phoneNumberDocId"]
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/whatsapp/calling?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "phoneNumberDocId": "66f6c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f3",
  "phoneNumber": "+14155550100",
  "callingEnabled": false,
  "callDeepLink": null,
  "forwardTo": null,
  "recordingEnabled": false,
  "sipAuthUsername": null,
  "sipAuthPasswordConfigured": false,
  "callerIdMode": "business",
  "callerIdVerified": true,
  "maxCallDurationSeconds": null,
  "forwardCallerId": "business"
}
```

## Step 2: Enable calling

Call `POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/whatsapp/calling` with `accountId` and `forwardTo`. Zernio sets `calling.status=ENABLED` on Meta, stores the Meta-issued SIP password encrypted, and snapshots the destination.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: enabled } = await zernio.whatsappcalling.enableWhatsAppCalling({
  path: { id: phoneNumberId },
  body: {
    accountId,
    forwardTo: 'tel:+13105559876',
    recordingEnabled: false
  }
});

console.log(enabled.callingEnabled);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
enabled = client.whatsapp_calling.enable_whats_app_calling(
    id=phone_number_id,
    account_id=account_id,
    forward_to="tel:+13105559876",
    recording_enabled=False,
)

print(enabled["callingEnabled"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/66f6c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f3/whatsapp/calling" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "forwardTo": "tel:+13105559876", "recordingEnabled": false}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "callingEnabled": true,
  "forwardTo": "tel:+13105559876",
  "callerIdMode": "business"
}
```

Optional settings:

- **Recording** is off by default. With `recordingEnabled: true` a consent prompt plays before recording starts and the per-minute surcharge applies.
- `maxCallDurationSeconds` caps a forwarded call, so a destination that never hangs up cannot bill dead air.
- On the [balance](/pricing/balance), calls are also capped by what the balance, plus what auto top-up can still add this month, pays for. Inbound calls always get at least 10 minutes, except a forward to a phone number, which is not made under one minute.
- `forwardCallerId: "caller"` presents the WhatsApp user's number to a `sip:` destination instead of yours.

After enabling, `callDeepLink` on the config is a public `https://wa.me/call/...` link. It starts a WhatsApp call to the number from a website, email or QR code.

Change the destination or the recording flag later with `PATCH /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/whatsapp/calling` and the same body shape.

Turn calling off with `DELETE /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/whatsapp/calling?accountId=...`. Disabling keeps `forwardTo` and the SIP credentials, so re-enabling needs no reconfiguration.

## Step 3: Check call permission

WhatsApp requires the customer to allow calls before you dial them. Call `GET /v1/whatsapp/call-permissions` with `accountId` and `to`.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: permission } = await zernio.whatsappcalling.getWhatsAppCallPermissions({
  query: { accountId, to: '+13105551234' }
});

console.log(permission.permission.status);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
permission = client.whatsapp_calling.get_whats_app_call_permissions(
    account_id=account_id,
    to="+13105551234",
)

print(permission["permission"]["status"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/whatsapp/call-permissions?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d&to=%2B13105551234" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "permission": { "status": "no_permission" },
  "actions": [
    { "action_name": "send_call_permission_request", "can_perform_action": true },
    { "action_name": "start_call", "can_perform_action": false }
  ]
}
```

`status` is `permanent`, `temporary` (with `expiration_time` in Unix seconds) or `no_permission`.

When `start_call` is not allowed, send the consent prompt with `POST /v1/whatsapp/calls` and `action: "send_call_permission_request"` (optionally `bodyText`). The customer taps Allow in WhatsApp.

Meta limits the prompt to 1 per customer per 24 hours and 2 per 7 days. It needs an open 24-hour service window.

## Step 4: Place an outbound call

Call `POST /v1/whatsapp/calls` with `accountId` and `to`. The call bridges to the number's `forwardTo` unless you pass a per-call `forwardTo` override.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retry replays the response instead of dialing, and billing, a second call.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: call } = await zernio.whatsappcalling.initiateWhatsAppCall({
  body: { accountId, to: '+13105551234' }
});

console.log(call.callId, call.status);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
call = client.whatsapp_calling.initiate_whats_app_call(
    account_id=account_id,
    to="+13105551234",
)

print(call["callId"], call["status"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/whatsapp/calls" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3f1c9d2e-7b4a-4e8f-9c0d-1a2b3c4d5e6f" \
  -d '{"accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "to": "+13105551234"}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "callId": "66f8e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b5",
  "status": "dialing",
  "direction": "outbound",
  "to": "+13105551234",
  "forwardTo": "tel:+13105559876",
  "recordingEnabled": false
}
```

The rest of the call's life arrives on the [call webhooks](/webhooks/phone).

Hang up with `POST /v1/voice/calls/{callId}/end`, the same endpoint as [voice calls](/platforms/voice/outbound#transfer-and-hang-up).

It ends the call whether it is still ringing or already answered. It works for outbound calls and for inbound ones (`call.id` on the `call.received` webhook).

A call forwarded to a `wss://` destination also ends when your WebSocket closes. Dropping the socket stops the call and its billing.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/voice/calls/66f8e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b5/end" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

## Step 5: Read call history

Call `GET /v1/whatsapp/calls` with `accountId`, optionally filtered by `status`, `direction`, `since` and `until`.

Each call carries its duration, end reason, recording URL when recording was on, and a billing breakdown.

Pass the returned `nextCursor` as `before` for the next page.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: history } = await zernio.whatsappcalling.listWhatsAppCalls({
  query: { accountId, direction: 'inbound', limit: 50 }
});

for (const c of history.calls) {
  console.log(c.direction, c.status, c.durationSeconds, c.billing?.billableCostUSD);
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
history = client.whatsapp_calling.list_whats_app_calls(
    account_id=account_id,
    direction="inbound",
    limit=50,
)

for c in history["calls"]:
    print(c["direction"], c["status"], c.get("durationSeconds"), c.get("billing", {}).get("billableCostUSD"))
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/whatsapp/calls?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d&direction=inbound&limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "calls": [
    {
      "_id": "66f8e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b5",
      "direction": "inbound",
      "from": "+13105551234",
      "to": "+14155550100",
      "status": "ended",
      "startedAt": "2027-01-01T09:00:00Z",
      "endedAt": "2027-01-01T09:04:12Z",
      "durationSeconds": 252,
      "endReason": "hangup",
      "billing": {
        "metaCostUSD": 0,
        "telnyxCostUSD": 0.0336,
        "recordingCostUSD": 0,
        "billableCostUSD": 0.0672,
        "totalCostUSD": 0.0672,
        "currency": "USD"
      }
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `billing.telnyxCostUSD`, `billing.recordingCostUSD` | The raw upstream costs |
| `billing.billableCostUSD` | What Zernio bills for them, at the published [call rate](/pricing/phone) |
| `billing.metaCostUSD` | Meta's per-minute fee, billed by Meta directly to your WABA and shown for reference only |

Inbound calls carry no Meta fee, which is why `metaCostUSD` is `0` here.

## If it fails

A `409` from `POST /v1/whatsapp/calls` means the customer has not allowed calls:

```json
{
  "error": "No active call permission. Send a permission request first."
}
```

Run Step 3, send the permission request, and dial once `start_call` is allowed.

A `422` means one of:

- calling is not enabled on the number
- the number's country blocks business-initiated calls
- the Meta SIP credentials are missing

A `402` with `code: "insufficient_balance"` means your balance cannot fund one minute of the call. Add funds at `funding_url`, then retry.

A `502` means the carrier could not originate the call, and it was marked `failed`.

Every error uses the envelope in [error handling](/guides/error-handling).
